header.title: Storage
header.subtitle: ZFS pool health, capacity, redundancy, disk temperatures, alerts and snapshots across your storage appliances, with staged changes.

empty.title: No storage appliances yet
empty.description: Connect a TrueNAS appliance to see pool health, capacity, disks and alerts in one place.

writes.needWs: Changes need the WebSocket JSON-RPC API (TrueNAS SCALE 25.04 or later). This appliance answered on the older REST API.

snapshots.truncated: Showing the {{shown}} most recent of {{total}}. Search the appliance for older ones.
snapshots.empty: No snapshots yet. Take one from the Datasets table above.

stage.failedDetail: The change was not staged. Try again.

snapshotDialog.title: Take a snapshot
snapshotDialog.description: A point-in-time snapshot of {{dataset}}. It adds a restore point and changes nothing on disk.
snapshotDialog.recursiveDescription: Snapshot every dataset nested under this one, atomically.

datasetDialog.title: Create a dataset
datasetDialog.description: A new ZFS dataset. Give a path inside the pool, such as backups or media/photos, not a /mnt path.

scrubDialog.title: Start a scrub on {{pool}}?
scrubDialog.description: A scrub checks every block in the pool against its checksum and repairs what it can. It is safe but reads the whole pool, so it runs in the background for a while, and this page shows its progress. This stages the request for you to apply.

deleteSnapshotDialog.title: Delete this snapshot?
deleteSnapshotDialog.description: <mono>{{snapshot}}</mono> is destroyed when you apply the change. The dataset and its live data are not touched: only this restore point is removed, and only after you apply.

addDialog.title: Add TrueNAS Storage
addDialog.description: Connect a TrueNAS SCALE or CORE appliance to see pool health, capacity and disks. Adding it changes nothing on the appliance.
addDialog.heading: TrueNAS Storage
addDialog.testNeedsFields: Enter the host, the API key owner and the API key to test the connection.
addDialog.name: Name
addDialog.keyOwnerHelp: The login-enabled account the API key belongs to. On TrueNAS 25.x the root account is disabled by default; use truenas_admin.
addDialog.apiKeyHelp: The connection always uses TLS: TrueNAS revokes any key it sees over plaintext. A read-only key is enough to monitor the appliance; applying staged changes needs a key that can write.
addDialog.verifyTlsHelp: Turn off for the appliance's default self-signed certificate.
addDialog.writesNote: FreeSDN reads pool health, capacity, disks, datasets and snapshots. A snapshot, dataset or scrub you start from the Storage page is staged in Pending Changes and reaches the appliance only when you apply it.
